title: UK CPI, January 2027 (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET) — the print that carries the January Ofgem cap step, and the last UK inflation reading fully inside the electricity VAT zero rate
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/consumerpriceinflationukjanuary2027, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — the ONS release-calendar entry reads verbatim 'Consumer price inflation, UK: January 2027', '17 February 2027 7:00am', and is marked 'This release is not yet published.' Filed estimate on the taxonomy gap (market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix list has no slot for a foreign national statistics institute — the same count every other UK entry on this calendar is filed under) and on this lane's no-self-confirm limit. The DATE is ONS's own scheduled slot and is not in doubt. Discovered 2026-09-09 during the never-assessed initial research of ofgem-price-cap-announcement-2026-11-25
notes: PROPOSED BY THE ofgem-price-cap-announcement-2026-11-25 LANE, 2026-09-09. It is the scoring venue for the Ofgem announcement, which is why the announcement lane rather than a CPI lane found it: the Ofgem cap steps on 1 January, and the first ONS observation of that step is the January bulletin on 2027-02-17. Nothing measurable happens on 1 January itself. TWO ATTRIBUTION RULES THE PRINT NEEDS. (1) The step is VAT-CLEAN. Domestic electricity in Great Britain is zero-rated 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027 (SI 2026/987, uk-electricity-vat-zero-rate-2026-10-01), so both the Oct-Dec 2026 and Jan-Mar 2027 cap periods sit inside the zero rate and the January cap step is pure wholesale, network and policy cost — not tax. Read a hot January electricity contribution as energy, not as a tax change. (2) It is the LAST UK inflation reading fully inside the zero rate; the reversion on 2027-04-01 (uk-electricity-vat-reversion-2027-04-01) reappears as an upward base effect in the April 2027 print (~2027-05-19, already proposed by that lane). Cornwall Insight's live forecast at proposal time was a 9% January cap rise to about GBP 1,872 (26 August 2026), driven by Middle East conflict, a European heatwave, Norwegian supply disruption and low winter gas stocks — with roughly nine weeks of Ofgem's observation window still to run, so the magnitude was unsettled and only the direction was leanable. It also lands two days AFTER the 2027-02-15 US market closure and the day the Apr-Jun cap window is already open, but no UK print reaches this book: symbols [], and the calendar's universe is eight US mega-caps with no UK listing, gilt or sterling instrument. Tiered LOW on that ground alone. Estimate widens caution only.
